summary: You take PSYCH 1 and PSYCH 10, three core courses with at least one from each of Areas A and B, and electives of 3 or more units, for 35 units, each letter graded with a C- or better unless it is offered only S/NC. Electives are PSYCH courses or the cognates BIO 150, PSYC 135 and PSYC 139; independent study, research and practica do not count. A comparable statistics course in place of PSYCH 10 is moved in by hand, and the rules against AP credit, summer-quarter Psychology courses and courses taken elsewhere are checked by hand.

program.why: Grading: "All courses towards the 35-unit requirement must be taken for a letter grade of C- or better, except for courses offered only on a satisfactory/no credit basis."

3X06XTQi.why: "Completing a minimum of 35 units in Psychology is required for the minor" is program.unitsMin; "All courses used to fulfill the minor's requirements must be taken at Stanford ... and passed with a grade of C- or better, except for courses offered only on a satisfactory/no credit basis" is program.minGrade (the audit already accepts S for S/NC-only courses). Summer-quarter and where-taken limits cannot be checked.

0U31lWK2.why: "The remaining unit requirements can be fulfilled through elective PSYCH courses ... An elective Psychology course is any PSYCH course offered for three units or more (excluding independent study, research, and practicum). There are three cognate courses from other departments that count towards the major as PSYCH elective units: BIO 150, PSYC 135, and PSYC 139." Overview: "Independent study, research, and practice cannot be counted toward the minor." The 35 units are program.unitsMin; this pool takes the rest. The excluded courses are the PSYCH courses whose catalog titles name them as independent study, research projects or practica.

add.why: "three of ten core courses with a minimum of one from each of two areas": the third core course, from either area.
